draft.title: Allotropes
card: Allotropes are different forms of the same element in the same state. Their atoms are joined in different arrangements, so their properties differ.
Diamond
each carbon atom is bonded to four others in a rigid 3D network. It is very hard and does not conduct electricity, as it has no free electrons.
Graphite
each carbon atom is bonded to three others in flat layers. The layers can slide over each other, so graphite is soft. It conducts electricity, as each atom has one electron free to move.
Fullerenes
carbon atoms joined in hollow cages or tubes, such as the ball-shaped C60. These are separate molecules, not a giant network.
draft.remember: Same element, different arrangement of atoms, different properties.

a.q: Why are diamond and graphite called allotropes of carbon?
opts: They are different structural forms of the same element
They are different elements that both bond to carbon
They have the same structure but different melting points
They are compounds made of carbon and another element
a.why: Both are made only of carbon atoms, joined in different arrangements. Having different properties does not make them allotropes by itself: the same element in different structures is what matters.
a.clue: Think about what atoms each one is made of.

b.q: Graphite is used in pencils and conducts electricity, but diamond does not conduct. What best explains the difference?
opts: Graphite has a free electron per atom, but diamond has none
Graphite has ions that move, but diamond has none
Graphite has four bonds per atom, but diamond has three
Graphite is a different element from diamond
b.why: In graphite each carbon atom bonds to three others, leaving one electron free to move between layers. In diamond all four outer electrons are held in bonds. The element is the same in both, so a different element cannot be the reason.
b.clue: Compare how many bonds each carbon atom makes in the two forms.

a.best: They are different structural forms of the same element

b.best: Graphite has a free electron per atom, but diamond has none

problems.detail: Why (b) says graphite's free electron moves 'between layers'. The delocalised electrons move along (within) the layers, which is why graphite conducts well parallel to the layers and poorly across them. It should say 'along the layers'.
